newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE bans collection of funds by charities.
newsitem.headline: UAE bans collection of funds by charities.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates on Sunday banned the collection of funds by charities, in an apparent move to halt the flow of some cash to Islamist groups accused of being "terrorist" organisations.

The oil state's Justice, Islamic Affairs and Endowments Minister Mohammad Nakhira al-Zahiri ordered a ban on the issuance of licences for the collection of donations, the official WAM news agency reported.

Zahiri said the ban was aimed at closing the door to those who tried "to make financial gains under the name of religion", while the state provided special care for the needy through existing organisations and societies that enjoyed government subsidies.
Official sources said the measure was a blanket ban, but some organisations like the UAE's Red Crescent Society could in future operate under new regulations.

Several Gulf Arab states have received requests from regional and Western allies to monitor operations by some Moslem charities, saying that some funds ended up in the hands of "terrorist" groups, Arab and Western officials said.
"Not all the money goes to such people, but sometimes mistakes happen and money ends up in wrong hands," said a Gulf Arab source.

Citizens and Gulf Arab governments are known to donate funds generously to help fellow Moslems in other parts of the world like Bosnia, Chechnya and Afghanistan, but no official campaigns have been held on behalf of Arab or other groups accused of carrying out deadly attacks.
